title: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Chronicles (International Critical Commentary)

verification_log.method: pp. 501–502: Kings knows no reform before the eighteenth year; the Chronicler makes Josiah pious from his eighth year and moves the purge before the discovery because "such a pious king … must be represented as pious from his youth"; p. 503: harmonisation (Bertheau, Zöckler, Oettli) treats Kings as describing the consummation of an earlier reform; p. 511: since Josiah was slain at Megiddo, "in peace" suggests Huldah's words were written before his death — "a testimony to the genuineness of the prophecy"; pp. 516–518: Necho reigned 609–594; Carchemish is the "geographical goal" introduced from the defeat there two years later; Josiah probably acted to preserve Judah's independence; the embassy is "probably" a fiction; the death is modelled on Ahab's; the battle was at Megiddo not because Necho came by sea (against Cheyne) but as an old battle-ground; Chronicles says he died after reaching Jerusalem; an assassination reading of Kings is unlikely; Jeremiah's elegy is lost; the "lamentations" are not the canonical book; a reference in Zech 12:11 is "very doubtful"
